path: Torsion length of finitely presented groups

results.title: Torsion series
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a group $G$, the torsion series of Chiodo and Vyas is the sequence of subgroups $\mathrm{Tor}_i(G)$ of $G$ defined by $\mathrm{Tor}_0(G) = 1$, the trivial subgroup, and, for each $i$, $\mathrm{Tor}_{i+1}(G)$ is the normal closure in $G$ of the set of elements $g$ such that $g^n \in \mathrm{Tor}_i(G)$ for some integer $n > 0$.

results.title: Torsion length greater than two
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ has torsion length greater than $2$ when $G / \mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is not torsion-free, where $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is the second term of the torsion series of $G$: some element $g \in G$ outside $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ has a power $g^n$ with $n > 0$ in $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$.

results.title: Kourovka Problem 19.23 (Chiodo–Vyas), finitely presented form
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that there is a finitely presented soluble group $G$ of torsion length greater than $2$, that is, such that $G / \mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is not torsion-free, where $\mathrm{Tor}_2(G)$ is the second term of the torsion series of $G$.

results.title: Finitely presented soluble groups of torsion length greater than two
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Resolved true: the Kourovka Archive answers 19.23 "Yes, such groups exist"; Leary and Minasyan (Theorem 2.14) construct polycyclic groups, which are finitely presented and soluble, of every torsion length `n ≥ 1`, in particular of torsion length `3`. Source: E. I. Khukhro and V. D. Mazurov (eds.), Unsolved Problems in Group Theory: The Kourovka Notebook, 21st issue, arXiv:1401.0300v49 (2026), Archive of Solved…

results.title: Maximal condition on subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups when every subgroup of $G$ is finitely generated.

results.title: Minimal condition on subgroups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ satisfies the minimal condition on subgroups when the order on subgroups of $G$ by inclusion is well-founded: every nonempty set of subgroups of $G$ has a minimal element, equivalently there is no infinite strictly descending chain of subgroups of $G$.

results.title: Minimax groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is a minimax group when it has a finite subnormal series $1 = H_0 \le H_1 \le \dots \le H_n = G$, with each $H_i$ normal in $H_{i+1}$, such that every factor $H_{i+1}/H_i$ satisfies the maximal condition on subgroups or the minimal condition on subgroups.

results.title: Groups with the same finite images
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Two groups $G$ and $H$ have the same finite images when, for every finite group $Q$, there is a surjective homomorphism $G \to Q$ exactly when there is a surjective homomorphism $H \to Q$.

results.title: Residually finite groups
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A group $G$ is residually finite when for every element $g \ne 1$ of $G$ there is a normal subgroup $N$ of finite index in $G$ with $g \notin N$.

results.title: Minimax groups and finite images (Kourovka 12.90)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The statement that for all groups $G$ and $H$, if $G$ is a finitely generated soluble minimax group and $H$ is a finitely generated residually finite group with the same finite images as $G$ (a finite group is a homomorphic image of $G$ exactly when it is a homomorphic image of $H$), then $H$ is a minimax group.

results.title: Finite images determine minimaxity (Mann–Segal)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a finitely generated soluble minimax group and let $H$ be a finitely generated residually finite group with the same finite images as $G$: a finite group is a homomorphic image of $G$ exactly when it is a homomorphic image of $H$. Then $H$ is a minimax group.

results.title: Consecutive polynomial family
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $k$ be a natural number. A family $L_0, \dots, L_{k-1}$ of polynomials in $\mathbb{Z}[X]$ is consecutive when $L_{i+1} - L_i = 1$ for every $i$ with $i + 1 < k$.

results.title: Natural numbers with the same prime divisors
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Natural numbers $a$ and $b$ have the same prime support when every prime $p$ divides $a$ if and only if it divides $b$.

results.title: Right density zero at the origin
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A set $S \subseteq \mathbb{R}$ has right-hand density $0$ at $0$ if the Lebesgue outer measure of $S \cap (0, \delta]$, divided by $\delta$, tends to $0$ as $\delta \to 0^+$.

results.title: Approximate continuity
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A function $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ is approximately continuous at $x$ if, for every $\varepsilon > 0$, the set $S_\varepsilon = \{y : |f(y) - f(x)| < \varepsilon\}$ has density $1$ at $x$: the Lebesgue outer measure of $S_\varepsilon \cap (x - \delta, x + \delta)$, divided by $2\delta$, tends to $1$ as $\delta \to 0^+$.

results.title: Positive upper right approximate derivative
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The upper right-hand approximate derivative of $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ at $x$ is positive: there are $a > 0$ and $\varepsilon > 0$ such that for every $\delta > 0$ there is $\delta' \in (0, \delta]$ for which the Lebesgue outer measure of $\{h \in (0, \delta'] : (f(x + h) - f(x))/h > a\}$ is at least $\varepsilon \delta'$.

results.title: Approximate derivative test for monotonicity (Scottish Book Problem 157)
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $f \colon \mathbb{R} \to \mathbb{R}$ be approximately continuous at every point, and suppose that at every point $x$ the upper right-hand approximate derivative of $f$ is positive. Then $f$ is monotone nondecreasing.

results.title: Unique witnesses transported by finite-sum equality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: If every integer-valued sum over `T` pulls back to the corresponding sum over `s`, then a property with a unique witness in `T` pulls back to a property with a unique witness in `s`.

results.title: Density bounds transfer through equal-fiber maps

results.title: Claw-free finite graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a finite vertex set $V$ is claw-free if it has no induced claw $K_{1,3}$: there are no vertices $c, \ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3 \in V$ such that $\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3$ are pairwise distinct, each is adjacent to $c$ and different from $c$, and no two of them are adjacent.

results.title: Chudnovsky–Seymour theorem
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a claw-free simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $I(G) = \sum_{k=0}^{|V|} i_k X^k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be its independence polynomial, where $i_k$ is the number of independent sets of $G$ with $k$ vertices. results.title: Claw-free finite graphs have no induced claw
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set. Then $G$ is claw-free if and only if the claw $K_{1,3}$, the star graph on four vertices whose center is adjacent to the other three, is not an induced subgraph of $G$, that is, there is no injective map from its vertices to those of $G$ that preserves both adjacency and nonadjacency.

results.title: Coefficients of the independence polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $I(G) = \sum_{k=0}^{|V|} i_k X^k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be its independence polynomial, where $i_k$ is the number of independent sets of $G$ with $k$ vertices. Then for every natural number $k$, the coefficient of $X^k$ in $I(G)$ is the number of independent sets of $G$ with exactly $k$ vertices.

results.title: Evaluating the independence polynomial
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on a finite vertex set $V$, and let $I(G) = \sum_{k=0}^{|V|} i_k X^k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be its independence polynomial, where $i_k$ is the number of independent sets of $G$ with $k$ vertices. Then for every element $x$ of a commutative ring $R$, the value of $I(G)$ at $x$ is $\sum_S x^{|S|}$, the sum running over all independent sets $S \subseteq V$ of $G$, the empty set included.

results.title: Independence polynomial of the edgeless graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set. For a simple graph $G$ on $V$, let $I(G) = \sum_{k=0}^{|V|} i_k X^k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be its independence polynomial, where $i_k$ is the number of independent sets of $G$ with $k$ vertices. If $G$ is the graph on $V$ with no edges, then $I(G) = (1 + X)^{|V|}$.

results.title: Independence polynomial of the complete graph
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $V$ be a finite set. For a simple graph $G$ on $V$, let $I(G) = \sum_{k=0}^{|V|} i_k X^k \in \mathbb{Z}[X]$ be its independence polynomial, where $i_k$ is the number of independent sets of $G$ with $k$ vertices. If $G$ is the complete graph on $V$, then $I(G) = 1 + |V|\,X$.

results.title: Claw-free graph
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: A simple graph $G$ on a vertex set $V$, not necessarily finite, is claw-free if it has no induced claw $K_{1,3}$: there are no vertices $c, \ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3 \in V$ such that $\ell_1, \ell_2, \ell_3$ are pairwise distinct, each is adjacent to $c$ and different from $c$, and no two of them are adjacent.

results.title: Claw-free graphs have no induced claw
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on an arbitrary vertex set. Then $G$ is claw-free if and only if the claw $K_{1,3}$, the star graph on four vertices whose center is adjacent to the other three, is not an induced subgraph of $G$, that is, there is no injective map from its vertices to those of $G$ that preserves both adjacency and nonadjacency.

results.title: The two definitions of claw-free agree
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: A simple graph on a finite vertex set is a claw-free finite graph if and only if it is a claw-free graph in the sense defined for graphs on arbitrary vertex sets.

results.title: Aaronson-Wigderson: the algebrization barrier
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Call an oracle a function from bitstrings to booleans. There are oracles $B$ and $\tilde B$ such that $\tilde B$ is an algebraic extension of $B$ and $\mathsf{P}^B = \mathsf{NP}^{\tilde B}$. There are also oracles $B$ and $\tilde B$ such that $\tilde B$ is an algebraic extension of $B$ and $\mathsf{NP}^B$ is not contained in $\mathsf{P}^{\tilde B}$.
